angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 536,385 km at 182.05 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.4929 +/- 0.0176 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 182.05 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.771 +/- 0.039 solar radii from Heidari et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2537 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A..36H/abstract): 536,385 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.771 +/- 0.049 solar masses from Heidari et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2537 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A..36H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4870 +/- 150 K from Heidari et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2537 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A..36H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Heidari et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2537 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A..36H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2537.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.551, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
